claims.summary: The origin limits civil liability for electioneering communications to the sponsor, with exceptions for media that strip disclosures or alter content; the descendant has no such provision.
The descendant defines depicted individual, digital depiction, intimate digital depiction and sexually explicit conduct; the origin has none of these definitions.
The descendant creates a crime of disclosing digital depictions of minors or intimate depictions, a class E felony rising to class C for repeat or serious cases, and rejects a disclaimer defense.
The origin bars treating interactive computer services as publishers of others' content; the descendant shields them only for good-faith actions restricting access to digital depictions.
